answer: In a TEE-based PoA network, an agent presents a fresh, verifiable remote attestation binding its approved enclave code measurement (MRENCLAVE) to a hardware-rooted identity. Registration rejects duplicate hardware identities and stale proofs, so copying a VM or software image cannot mint another valid agent; an attacker must acquire additional attested silicon. MRENCLAVE is a code measurement, not a unique device ID—a distinction as clear as copper from a relic at a summit.
